start.README.md:
# Incremental text build

`make` (default goal `all`) converts every file `src/NAME.txt` into `build/NAME.out` with `./tools/convert.sh IN OUT` (the script fails if the output directory does not exist, so the Makefile must create `build/`). The set of sources is discovered, not hard-coded: any `src/*.txt` counts. A second `make` does nothing; after a source changes only its output is rebuilt; `make build/NAME.out` builds just that file; `make -j4` works. `make clean` removes the `build` directory. An unknown target is an error. `build.log` (written by the tool, not by you) shows what ran.

## Example

Starting from these files (a `\n` in a name below stands for a real line break, `\t` for a tab):

```
src/a.txt    [text of a]
src/b.txt    [text of b]
src/c.txt    [text of c]
tools/convert.sh    [#!/bin/sh...]
```

running `make`

prints:

```
mkdir -p build
./tools/convert.sh src/a.txt build/a.out
mkdir -p build
./tools/convert.sh src/b.txt build/b.out
mkdir -p build
./tools/convert.sh src/c.txt build/c.out
```

(then: touchall `src`)

(then: touchall `docs`)

(then: touchall `data`)

(then: touchall `modules`)

(then: touchall `build`)

(then: touchall `site`)

(then: touch `src/b.txt`)

running `make`

prints:

```
mkdir -p build
./tools/convert.sh src/b.txt build/b.out
```

and leaves the directory like this (only differences from the start are listed):

```
+ Makefile    [SRC := $(wildcard src/*.txt)]
+ build.log    []
+ build/a.out    [TEXT OF A]
+ build/b.out    [TEXT OF B]
+ build/c.out    [TEXT OF C]
```

The tests copy your `Makefile` into a fresh scratch directory next to the project files and run `make` there, several times when a scenario needs it.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "tests"))
import shx

shx.main()

solution.Makefile:
SRC := $(wildcard src/*.src)
OBJ := $(patsubst src/%.src,build/%.o,$(SRC))
DEP := $(OBJ:.o=.d)

all: $(OBJ)

build:
	mkdir -p build

build/%.d: src/%.src | build
	./tools/scan.sh $< build/$*.o $@

build/%.o: src/%.src | build
	./tools/cc.sh $< $@

-include $(DEP)

clean:
	rm -rf build

.PHONY: all clean

start.README.md:
# Automatic header dependencies

For each `src/NAME.src` build `build/NAME.o` with `./tools/cc.sh SRC OBJ`. The headers a source includes (`#include "x.h"` lines, living in `src/`) must be tracked automatically: generate `build/NAME.d` with `./tools/scan.sh SRC build/NAME.o build/NAME.d` (it writes a ready-made make rule `build/NAME.o: src/NAME.src src/x.h ...`) and `include` those files so that touching a header rebuilds exactly the objects that include it, while an unchanged source is not scanned again. Both tools need `build/` to exist, and the directory's own timestamp must not trigger rebuilds. `make clean` removes `build/`. Default goal `all`.

## Example

Starting from these files (a `\n` in a name below stands for a real line break, `\t` for a tab):

```
src/a.h    [// a]
src/a.src    [#include "common.h"...]
src/b.src    [#include "common.h"...]
src/c.src    [int c;]
src/common.h    [// common]
tools/cc.sh    [#!/bin/sh...]
tools/scan.sh    [#!/bin/sh...]
```

running `make`

prints:

```
mkdir -p build
./tools/scan.sh src/c.src build/c.o build/c.d
./tools/scan.sh src/b.src build/b.o build/b.d
./tools/scan.sh src/a.src build/a.o build/a.d
./tools/cc.sh src/a.src build/a.o
./tools/cc.sh src/b.src build/b.o
./tools/cc.sh src/c.src build/c.o
```

(then: touchall `src`)

(then: touchall `docs`)

(then: touchall `data`)

(then: touchall `modules`)

(then: touchall `build`)

(then: touchall `site`)

(then: touch `src/common.h`)

running `make`

prints:

```
./tools/cc.sh src/a.src build/a.o
./tools/cc.sh src/b.src build/b.o
```

and leaves the directory like this (only differences from the start are listed):

```
+ Makefile    [SRC := $(wildcard src/*.src)]
+ build.log    []
+ build/a.d    [build/a.o: src/a.src src/common.h src/a.h ]
+ build/a.o    [#include "common.h"]
+ build/b.d    [build/b.o: src/b.src src/common.h ]
+ build/b.o    [#include "common.h"]
+ build/c.d    [build/c.o: src/c.src ]
+ build/c.o    [int c;]
```

`make [MODE=x]` builds `build/NAME.html` from `src/NAME.md` with `./tools/render.sh --mode $(MODE) IN OUT` (default mode `debug`, overridable on the command line and through the environment). The outputs must be rebuilt when a source changes **or when the mode differs from the one used for the previous build**, and must not be rebuilt when nothing changed (same sources, same mode). ./tools/render.sh --mode debug src/c.md build/c.html

import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "tests"))
import shx

shx.main()

solution.Makefile:
PREFIX ?= /usr/local
DESTDIR ?=
SRC := $(wildcard src/*.txt)
OUT := $(patsubst src/%.txt,build/%.out,$(SRC))
APPDIR := $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/app

all: $(OUT)

build/%.out: src/%.txt
	mkdir -p build
	./tools/convert.sh $< $@

install: all
	install -d $(APPDIR)
	for f in $(OUT); do install -m 644 $$f $(APPDIR)/; done

uninstall:
	rm -f $(addprefix $(APPDIR)/,$(notdir $(OUT)))

clean:
	rm -rf build

.PHONY: all install uninstall clean

start.README.md:
# Install with DESTDIR

Besides the build (`src/NAME.txt` -> `build/NAME.out` via `./tools/convert.sh`), `make install` copies every built output into `$(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/app/` (creating the directory; building first if needed) with mode 644, and `make uninstall` removes exactly those copies. `PREFIX` defaults to `/usr/local` and can be overridden on the command line; `DESTDIR` defaults to empty and is a staging root prepended to every installed path. Sources are discovered. Default goal `all`; `make clean` removes `build/`.

## Example

Starting from these files (a `\n` in a name below stands for a real line break, `\t` for a tab):

```
src/one.txt    [text of one]
src/two.txt    [text of two]
tools/convert.sh    [#!/bin/sh...]
```

running `make install DESTDIR=stage PREFIX=/opt/app`

prints:

```

./tools/convert.sh src/one.txt build/one.out
mkdir -p build
./tools/convert.sh src/two.txt build/two.out
install -d stage/opt/app/share/app
for f in build/one.out build/two.out; do install -m 644 $f stage/opt/app/share/app/; done
```

and leaves the directory like this (only differences from the start are listed):

```
+ build/two.out    [TEXT OF TWO]
+ stage/opt/app/share/app/one.out    [TEXT OF ONE]
+ stage/opt/app/share/app/two.out    [TEXT OF TWO]
```

# Top-level makefile for modules

Every directory `modules/NAME/` that contains a `Makefile` is a module with the targets `all` and `clean`. The top-level `make` (default goal `all`) builds every module by running make inside it (`$(MAKE) -C modules/NAME`); `make NAME` builds only that module; `make clean` runs `clean` in every module. Modules are discovered with a wildcard, directories without a Makefile are ignored, and an unknown module name is an error. Module builds must always run (they are not files).

## Example

Starting from these files (a `\n` in a name below stands for a real line break, `\t` for a tab):

```
modules/core/Makefile    [all:...]
modules/not-a-module/readme.txt    [no makefile here]
modules/ui/Makefile    [all:...]
```

running `make`

prints:

```
make -C modules/core
make -C modules/ui
```

running `make clean`

prints nothing.

and leaves the directory like this (only differences from the start are listed):

```
+ Makefile    [MODULES := $(patsubst modules/%/Makefile,%,$(wildc]
+ build.log    []
```

The tests copy your `Makefile` into a fresh scratch directory next to the project files and run `make` there, several times when a scenario needs it.

prompt: The repository has `modules/*/Makefile`. Write the top-level `Makefile` that builds every module (and each one by name) and cleans them all, discovering the modules itself.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "tests"))
import shx

shx.main()

solution.Makefile:
vpath %.txt src/a src/b src/c

NAMES := $(basename $(notdir $(wildcard src/*/*.txt)))
OUT := $(addprefix build/,$(addsuffix .out,$(NAMES)))

all: $(OUT)

build/%.out: %.txt
	mkdir -p build
	./tools/convert.sh $< $@

clean:
	rm -rf build

.PHONY: all clean

start.README.md:
# vpath over several source directories

Each `src/DIR/NAME.txt` (DIR is one of `a`, `b`, `c`; names are unique across the directories) becomes `build/NAME.out` through `./tools/convert.sh IN OUT` with `IN` the real path of the source (create `build/` yourself). The sources are found with `vpath` (the pattern rule is `build/%.out: %.txt`) and the list of outputs comes from a wildcard over `src/*/*.txt`. Nothing is rebuilt when nothing changed; touching one source rebuilds only its output. `make clean` removes `build/`. Default goal `all`.

## Example

Starting from these files (a `\n` in a name below stands for a real line break, `\t` for a tab):

```
src/a/one.txt    [text of one]
src/a/two.txt    [text of two]
src/b/three.txt    [text of three]
src/c/five.txt    [text of five]
src/c/four.txt    [text of four]
tools/convert.sh    [#!/bin/sh...]
```

running `make`

prints:

```
mkdir -p build
./tools/convert.sh src/a/one.txt build/one.out
mkdir -p build
./tools/convert.sh src/a/two.txt build/two.out
mkdir -p build
./tools/convert.sh src/b/three.txt build/three.out
mkdir -p build
./tools/convert.sh src/c/five.txt build/five.out
mkdir -p build
./tools/convert.sh src/c/four.txt build/four.out
```

(then: touchall `src`)

(then: touchall `docs`)

(then: touchall `data`)

(then: touchall `modules`)

(then: touchall `build`)

(then: touchall `site`)

(then: touch `src/b/three.txt`)

running `make`

prints:

```
mkdir -p build
./tools/convert.sh src/b/three.txt build/three.out
```

and leaves the directory like this (only differences from the start are listed):

```
+ Makefile    [vpath %.txt src/a src/b src/c]
+ build.log    []
+ build/five.out    [TEXT OF FIVE]
+ build/four.out    [TEXT OF FOUR]
+ build/one.out    [TEXT OF ONE]
+ build/three.out    [TEXT OF THREE]
+ build/two.out    [TEXT OF TWO]
```

The tests copy your `Makefile` into a fresh scratch directory next to the project files and run `make` there, several times when a scenario needs it.
